properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 2:48AM MDT until October 27 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Colorado...

Rio Grande At Alamosa affecting Alamosa County.

For the Upper Rio Grande...including Alamosa...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Alamosa.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor flooding. Minor agricultural flooding
in low lying areas along the river

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 AM MDT Monday the stage was 9.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 AM MDT Monday was 9.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.0 feet
this morning. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 10.0
feet on 05/23/1948.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 1:08AM MDT until October 27 at 1:15AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 115 AM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 103 AM MDT, Gauge reports indicated high stream flows.
Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the warned
area.
- Water levels continues to remain elevated within the Conejos
River near Manassa. In addition, Widespread inundation of
agriculture fields, wetlands, and other low-lying areas.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Manassa, Sanford, Antonito, Romeo, Conejos, Bountiful and Ortiz.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 2:07PM MDT until October 27 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Catastrophic flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected along the San Juan River between Four Corners and Mexican
Hat. This is an emergency situation!

* WHERE...Western Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 600 AM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along San Juan River is occurring or expected to
begin shortly. The crest will occur around Aneth, Montezuma Creek
and Bluff this afternoon and evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 204 PM MDT, Sunday the stage for the San Juan river near Bluff
was 20 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon to a crest of 29.5 feet early Monday morning. It will
then fall below flood stage early Tuesday morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 32.0
feet on 09/10/1927.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Tselakai Dezza, Bluff, Halchita, Montezuma Creek and
Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 9:00AM MDT until October 27 at 9:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall which occurred over
the last couple of days is expected or ongoing.

* WHERE...Northeastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...
Southwestern Alamosa County in southeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will occur in low-lying and flood-prone
locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 852 AM MDT, flooding was occurring along the Rio Grande River
in low lying and agricultural areas. This high water is due to
all of the heavy rain which occurred over the last couple of
days.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include low lying
areas in parts of Alamosa and parts of Conejos counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
